faqs.q: What are the Char-Lynn 101 Series Hydraulic Motors and what are they used for?
faqs.a: The Char-Lynn 101 Series Hydraulic Motors are a low-speed, high-torque orbital hydraulic motor, listed in 31 part numbers with displacement 2.8 to 22.6 in³/rev. Orbital motors suit machine drives that need torque at low shaft speed, and displacement sets the trade between speed and torque. The mounting is 4 Bolt Std / 1.748 Dia / .120 Pilot, 2 Bolt / SAE A / 3.25" Pilot, 2 Bolt / SAE B / 4.00" Pilot.

faqs.q: How do I identify the part number of the Char-Lynn 101 Series Hydraulic Motors?
faqs.a: Quote the part number from the motor nameplate, which carries the model code. For example 101-1001-009 (2.8 in³/rev, Keyed 1.00" shaft, 4 Bolt Std / 1.748 Dia / .120 Pilot mount, NPT - 1/2" ports) and 101-1032-009 (22.6 in³/rev, Keyed 1.00" shaft, 2 Bolt / SAE A / 3.25" Pilot mount, NPT - 1/2" ports) are two of the 31 rows. The size table gives the displacement, shaft and port details for each part number.

faqs.q: What displacement range do the Char-Lynn 101 Series Hydraulic Motors cover?
faqs.a: The Char-Lynn 101 Series Hydraulic Motors spans 2.8 to 22.6 in³/rev across 31 part numbers. That is 9 distinct displacements. A larger displacement turns slower with more torque for a given flow, and shaft speed in rpm is roughly flow in US gpm × 231 ÷ displacement in in³/rev, before volumetric losses.

faqs.q: Which shaft options do the Char-Lynn 101 Series Hydraulic Motors offer?
faqs.a: The shaft options on the Char-Lynn 101 Series Hydraulic Motors are Keyed 1.00", 1" Shaft / .406 Crosshole. Match the shaft to the machine, because keyed, spline and tapered shafts do not interchange. Give us the shaft type and diameter from your old motor, and the part number if you have it.
